# SurveyDokum

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

SurveyDokum helps you document survey datasets without writing everything by
hand. It works in two stages:

1. **R computes.** The package reads your data, flags missing-value codes,
   detects each variable's role (ID, Likert item, categorical, continuous,
   open text, date, weight) and computes the statistics that fit that role.
   These steps are deterministic and give the same result every time.
2. **A local language model writes.** The statistics are turned into a prompt,
   and a model running on your own machine through [Ollama](https://ollama.com/)
   writes a readable description of the dataset and the roxygen2 text for its
   R help page, in Finnish, English or Swedish.

The model only ever sees aggregate statistics. Individual responses, and the
text of open-ended answers in particular, are never included in a prompt, and
nothing is sent to an external service.

On top of that, SurveyDokum produces an HTML codebook, exports a DDI Codebook
2.6 XML file for archiving, and keeps the documentation up to date when new
variables or respondents are added.

**New to the package?** The [visual overview](overview.html) shows the whole
workflow on one page (also [suomeksi](yleiskuva.html) and
[på svenska](oversikt.html)).

## Installation

SurveyDokum is not on CRAN. Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("your-github-user/SurveyDokum")
```

The language-model steps also need Ollama installed and running, with a model
pulled, for example:

``` sh
ollama pull gemma3:12b
```

## Example: from data to statistics

This part runs in plain R, without a language model. It uses the example
dataset that ships with the package, a workplace wellbeing survey with 200
respondents. To keep the output short, we take five of its 17 variables.

```{r example}
library(SurveyDokum)

# sd_read() accepts csv, tsv, xlsx, xls, sav, dta and rds files.
# Here we save part of the example data as .rds so there is a file to read.
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(
  survey_data[, c("vastaaja_id", "sukupuoli", "tyovuodet", "tt1", "avoin_palaute")],
  path
)

aineisto <- sd_read(path)
aineisto <- sd_detect_roles(aineisto)
aineisto$meta$roles
```

The detected roles decide which statistics are computed. For the open-ended
variable `avoin_palaute`, only the number of distinct answers and their average
length are reported, never the answers themselves:

```{r summary}
sd_summarise(aineisto)
```

The statistics text is currently always in Finnish. The `language` argument
only changes the language of the text the model writes.

## Example: letting the model write

These steps need a running Ollama. Model output should always be reviewed
before it is saved, so the functions that write files only preview by default
(`dry_run = TRUE`).

```{r llm, eval = FALSE}
sd_check_ollama(model = "gemma3:12b")

# A readable description of the dataset
description <- sd_document(aineisto, language = "en")
print(description)

# Follow-up questions in the same conversation
description$chat$chat("Which items have the highest mean?")

# roxygen2 documentation for the ?survey_data help page
sd_generate_roxygen(aineisto, "survey_data", language = "en")   # preview
sd_generate_roxygen(aineisto, "survey_data", language = "en", dry_run = FALSE)
```

## Example: codebooks

```{r codebook, eval = FALSE}
sd_codebook(aineisto)                           # inst/codebook/codebook.html
sd_export_ddi(aineisto, file = "codebook.xml")  # DDI Codebook 2.6
```

## Keeping documentation up to date

```{r update, eval = FALSE}
# New variables: describe only those, keep the reviewed text
sd_check_documentation_current(aineisto, "survey_data")
sd_update_roxygen(aineisto, "survey_data", dry_run = FALSE)

# New respondents: fix the row count, no language model needed
sd_check_row_count(aineisto, "survey_data")
sd_update_row_count(aineisto, "survey_data", dry_run = FALSE)
```

## Learn more

The guides walk through setting up a documentation package for your own
dataset, from start to publishing a website. Each guide is available in three
languages:

- **Getting started**: [English](articles/getting-started.html),
  [suomeksi](articles/kayttoonotto.html),
  [på svenska](articles/kom-igang.html)
- **Using RAG** (adding background from your own reference material):
  [English](articles/using-rag.html),
  [suomeksi](articles/ragin-kaytto.html),
  [på svenska](articles/anvanda-rag.html)

Every function has its own help page, for example `?sd_read`,
`?sd_detect_roles` and `?sd_document`.
